key_insight: The paper shows that local energy transfer in turbulence can be decomposed geometrically into strain self-amplification and vortex stretching, with a spherical moment-of-inertia coefficient tying cascade strength to fluid-element deformation.
engineering_relevance: This gives a mechanistic, physics-based way to interpret and model forward versus inverse energy transfer in turbulence, which is useful for turbulence modeling and analysis in CFD and fluid engineering.
method: Derive an exact real-space energy-transfer decomposition at scale ℓ using spherical geometry.
Split the transfer into strain self-amplification and vortex-stretching contributions.
Further separate longitudinal and transverse components to link Kolmogorov’s 4/5-law transfer to strain dynamics.
evidence_signal: Direct numerical simulations confirm that the derived local contribution captures the dominant transfer and statistically separates forward-cascade from inverse-cascade events.
watch_item: The decomposition is exact for the idealized spherical neighborhood formulation, so applying it in practical simulations may require careful handling of finite-resolution, anisotropy, and non-spherical flow structures.
paper_title: Geometric Mechanics of Real-Space Energy Transfer in Turbulence
